tagline:
Archive your dream today.
Break it into steps you can do.
spoken: [hook] You don't need more willpower to stop checking your phone. You need more distance. || When it's on your desk, checking it takes one second. So your hand gets there before you've even decided to. || [turn] So for your first focused block, put your phone in another room, and close the door. Then set a timer on your laptop for twenty-five minutes. || Now checking it means standing up and walking away from your work. And that small pause is usually enough to keep you on the task. || Studying? One chapter, phone in the kitchen. Writing a report? The first page, phone in the bedroom. || When the timer ends, take five minutes. Check whatever you want, then start the next block. || [land] So before your next block, pick the room your phone goes to. One closed door does more than willpower ever will. || [outro] That's what Dmyor is for. You archive your dream today, so you can see it tomorrow, and break it down into small steps you can actually do. || [outro] If you want to try it out, I've put the link in the bio.
